title: Why Accountability Is Key To Building Rapport https://smartclassroommanagement.com/2012/08/04/why-accountability-is-key-to-building-rapport/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin argues that consistent accountability, not friendliness or leniency, is the true foundation of positive teacher-student relationships. He describes how a lack of accountability breeds brazen, disrespectful attitudes, pushing well-meaning teachers into resentment, sharpness, and the kind of confrontational teaching persona they never wanted to become. A fairly enforced classroom management plan, by contrast, protects students' right to learn, depersonalizes discipline so students blame only themselves, and builds trust by proving the teacher does what they say they'll do. He notes the surprising reward teachers get when they commit fully to this approach: students respond with gratitude, notes, and invitations rather than resistance. The piece closes by describing rapport as something that becomes effortless once accountability is firmly and fairly established.
points: Lack of accountability breeds brazen, disrespectful attitudes and pushes even well-meaning teachers toward resentment and sharpness.
A classroom management plan protects students' right to learn and depersonalizes discipline so misbehaving students blame only themselves.
Following through consistently on a management plan builds trust by proving a teacher does what they say they'll do.
Students respond to consistent accountability with unexpected gratitude — notes, smiles, invitations — rather than resistance.
Rapport becomes effortless once accountability is firmly and fairly established, without teachers having to work hard at building it.
quotes: When students aren’t held accountable for misbehavior, they take advantage of it. They become brazen and disrespectful.
The truth is, accountability is the foundation upon which positive relationships with students are built.
A classroom management plan is a contract between you and your students that protects their right to learn and enjoy school in a peaceful environment.
A classroom management plan allows you to hold students accountable for misbehavior without causing friction or resentment.
Following your classroom management plan builds trust between you and your students because in a very concrete way it shows them that you can be counted on to do what you say you’re going to do.
The biggest surprise to teachers who make the unwavering commitment to hold students accountable is the reaction they get from their students.
